leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members include programmable base editing without double-strand cleavage in their round-1 configuration; this is the only ballot ID that appears in more than two configurations. Brzezinski and Chabes make it their whole prize, while Aili, Aqvist, Linke and Somfai pair it with a second part. What is shared is the chemical reading (deaminase chemistry made programmable) and the view that it is distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize. What is not shared is the laureate set: Aili, Aqvist, Linke and Somfai name David R. Liu alone, while Brzezinski and Chabes name Liu, Alexis C. Komor and Nicole M. Gaudelli. Kondo and Nishida appear in no member's configuration, though several flag their parallel work.

Aqvist and Linke each propose a two-part prize pairing Liu for base editing with Shankar Balasubramanian and David Klenerman for massively parallel sequencing by synthesis based on reversible-terminator chemistry, framed as chemistry for rewriting and reading DNA. Both state that the sequencing citation would exclude Rothberg's pyrosequencing lineage and Mayer. They differ in that Aqvist explicitly moved toward this pairing after round-1 discussion, and both list the pairing's coherence and the technology-versus-chemistry question as open. Chabes and Somfai list B058 only as an alternative, and Aili names it as an alternative.

Aili alone proposes pairing Liu (base editing) with Craig M. Crews and Alessio Ciulli for PROTAC-based targeted protein degradation, a two-part chemical-biology prize. The PROTAC part omits Deshaies and the cereblon molecular-glue contributors (Handa, Ito), and Aqvist, Somfai and Chabes cite maturity and the PROTAC/glue split as reasons not to include it now.

Somfai alone proposes pairing Stephen L. Buchwald and John F. Hartwig for palladium-catalysed C-N coupling with Liu for base editing, to give a synthetic-methodology half and a chemistry-of-life half. Zou lists B054 as an alternative and Aqvist as a lower alternative, but no other member includes it in a configuration. Somfai notes that a trio on base editing would not fit beside a two-name B054 part under the three-person limit.

Sparr alone makes biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) her entire prize, as a general physical-chemical organizing principle. Aili, Brzezinski and Linke list it as an alternative or strong candidate but accept the maturity and attribution objections; Chabes and Zou question physiological evidence for in-cell condensates.

Zou alone makes halide perovskite solar absorbers (Miyasaka, Park, Snaith) her entire prize, as a new solution-processable materials class. Somfai explicitly ranks it below cross-coupling; Linke lists it only as an alternative; no other configuration contains it.

areas_of_agreement: Base editing is described by all six supporters as a chemical invention, deaminase chemistry directed to a programmed site without double-strand cleavage, and each who addresses it argues it is separable from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Liu is treated as the decisive figure in base editing by every member whose configuration includes it; no one proposes a base-editing citation that omits him.
Sequencing by synthesis, where discussed, is accepted as high-impact and mature; members disagree about how to cite it, not about its impact.
Several members (Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Somfai, Brzezinski) say the Kondo and Nishida Target-AID priority question should be checked against dates and not settled by omission.
Members who raise protein degradation (Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Somfai) agree that the PROTAC and cereblon molecular-glue strands are distinct discoveries.
Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke and Zou each say they value quantitative, reproduced evidence of a principle, and several members cite this when weighing maturity.
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing is a separate chemical advance or an engineering extension of CRISPR-Cas; Sparr and Zou press the second view, while Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke and Somfai argue the first.

Whether cytosine and adenine base editors are two distinct inventions (Brzezinski, Chabes, who note the adenine editor required evolving TadA to act on DNA) or one concept realized twice (Aqvist, Somfai, Aili, Linke, who name Liu alone).

Whether sequencing by synthesis belongs in a chemistry prize or is better described as genomics or technology; Zou and Aili raise this, Aqvist, Chabes and Linke point to reversible-terminator chemistry as real nucleotide chemistry.

Whether the in-cell reality of biomolecular condensates is established well enough; Sparr says the physical principle is sound, while Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke and Zou treat the in-cell evidence as still contested.
Whether Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a new chemical problem or an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize; Somfai and Zou differ from Aqvist's more relaxed reading in emphasis.
Whether Gray and Winkler's electron-transfer work adds a discovery beyond Marcus's 1992 prize; Brzezinski ranks it first, Aqvist, Linke and Sparr question it, and no other member includes it.
attribution_disputes: Base editing: Liu alone (Aili, Aqvist, Linke, Somfai) versus Liu with Komor and Gaudelli (Brzezinski, Chabes). Aili says she would reconsider if the adenine editor is judged a separate inventive step, and Aqvist could accept one trainee if argued from the primary papers.

Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) are named in no preferred configuration but are flagged by Aili, Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke, Somfai and Zou as a possible priority claim; Aili and Chabes note it is cytidine-deaminase only, while Linke and Brzezinski want dates verified.

Sequencing: Balasubramanian and Klenerman for reversible-terminator chemistry (Aqvist, Linke) versus a broader set including Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing lineage and Mayer's contribution, which Aqvist and Linke leave out and Aili and Brzezinski regard as an unresolved lineage choice.
Targeted degradation: Aili's Crews and Ciulli omits Deshaies and the Handa and Ito cereblon work; Aqvist's own degradation trio (Crews, Handa, Ciulli) differs from Aili's trio.
Phase separation: any three-person cut among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag omits Pappu and Mittag, which Sparr calls the weakest point of her case.
Perovskites: Zou's Miyasaka, Park and Snaith leaves out Gratzel, Kanatzidis and Seok, and Kojima does not appear in the credited names.
C-N coupling: Somfai and Zou agree Kosugi's tin-amide work is a precursor and should stay out.
maturity_disputes: Clinical maturity of base editing: Chabes, Brzezinski, Linke, Somfai and Zou note long-term safety (bystander edits, off-target deamination) is still accumulating, while supporters cite reproduction in many laboratories and early clinical use; several members state they recall clinical status from memory.
Protein degradation: Aili, Aqvist, Chabes and Somfai note no approved degrader from the core modality, which Aqvist and Chabes treat as a reason to defer.
Sequencing is described as arguably overdue (Aqvist, Chabes, Linke); Chabes adds that its maturity also means it can wait, whereas base editing is at the point of clinical validation.
Phase separation: members differ on whether about fifteen years of reproduction (Sparr) outweighs the open question of which assemblies are phase separated in vivo.
Perovskites: operational stability and lead toxicity are cited by Zou, Somfai and Linke as unresolved, and Zou notes much of the progress is device engineering.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Linke, Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues; each states this is not a tie to any shortlisted candidate.
Linke notes his nanophysics and molecular-motor research is adjacent to nanopore sensing (B026), which is in no member's configuration.
Somfai discloses a lean toward the synthetic-methodology candidate (B054) because of his own field.
Brzezinski discloses his role as Secretary and his link to Zou as a Stockholm University colleague, and his biophysical interest in electron transfer (B028), which does not bear on B018.
Aqvist discloses his connection to Warshel and the Uppsala ribosome community, relevant only to simulation candidates outside the configurations.
Chabes discloses topical closeness of his nucleotide metabolism and replication-fidelity work to base editing and sequencing chemistry, with no personal or institutional tie.
Aili and Sparr note scientific proximity in self-assembly and, for Sparr, lipid and amyloid assembly adjacent to condensates; Aili states this is not a personal tie.
No member discloses a conflict requiring recusal from any ballot in a preferred configuration.
questions_for_round2: For base editing, does the primary record support crediting Liu alone, or Liu with Komor and Gaudelli as lead experimentalists on the cytosine and adenine editor classes, and can the committee state the dates for Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID relative to the Liu laboratory's cytosine base editor?
Does the committee want base editing as a stand-alone prize or one part of a two-part prize, and if two parts, which second part (B058, B023 or B054) gives a citation explainable on its own terms?

If sequencing is included, can the committee justify citing Balasubramanian and Klenerman for reversible-terminator chemistry alone, and state in what sense it is new after Sanger in 1980, given Rothberg's 454 platform and Mayer's contribution?
Is the 2020 CRISPR prize a bar to base editing, and how should a citation word the distinction so that it names the chemical transformation of a base and not RNA-guided cleavage?

For B023, does the committee judge the chemical novelty to be the heterobifunctional degrader design or the cereblon glue mechanism, and does the absence of an approved degrader from the core modality settle the timing?

For B007, what is established beyond P-granule droplet behaviour that would let the citation credit the physical-chemical framework without the contested in-cell claims, and how should Pappu and Mittag be handled?

For B054 and B024, can members who rank them first state what each adds beyond the 2010 cross-coupling prize and beyond device engineering, and what do the members who did not rank them need to see before including them?
summary.chair_observation: The round-1 files show one clear point of overlap and no majority configuration. Six members include B018, but they split on laureates (Liu alone versus Liu, Komor and Gaudelli) and on whether it stands alone or is paired with B058, B023 or B054; Sparr (B007) and Zou (B024) place it only as an alternative. No other ballot ID appears in more than two configurations, and every member accompanies their preference with an explicit maturity or attribution reservation. Round 2 therefore turns largely on the base-editing attribution and priority record and on the choice of a second part, if any.
